newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish car output falls 11 pct in 1996 - auto group.
newsitem.headline: Turkish car output falls 11 pct in 1996 - auto group.

text.p: Turkey's car production fell to 207,757 last year, a drop of 11 percent from 233,412 in 1995, while December car output plunged 25 percent to 16,571 from 21,994 a year ago, the association of automotive industry (OSD) said on Thursday.
It said overall motor vehicle output firmed two percent to 325,467 in 1996 from 319,498 the previous year, but fell by 14 percent to 27,544 in December from 31,886 a year ago.
The second biggest output was in farm tractors with 48,720 units produced in 1996, up 31 percent, followed by 29,058 trucks which leapt 50 percent.
The 1996 output was 21,032 in pick-ups, up 25 percent, 10,171 in minibuses, up 33 percent, 5,856 midibuses, up 66 percent and 2,499 in buses, up 95 percent.
The OSD said 239,716 cars were sold in 1996, up 11 percent from 216,611 the previous year, due to a 165 percent surge in sales of imported cars to 57,479 in 1996 against 21,651.
Sales of locally produced cars dropped 6.5 percent to 182,237 last year from previous 194,960. The market share of imported cars jumped to 24 percent from 10 percent.
Car sales in Turkey peaked at 441,133 in 1993, including 340,063 domestic cars.

The OSD said domestic car sales firmed to 23,358 in December from 17,039 in November amid low-interest consumer loans and campaigns made to enliven weak demand as well as an increase in motor vehicle taxes due in January.
"But the higher December sale figure is expected to negatively affect car sales in January and February when sales usually hit bottom levels," the OSD added.
